authors: Abbes, Zouhaier and Trabelsi, Imen and Kharrat, Mohamed and Amri, Moez
title: Intercropping with fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) enhanced seed yield and reduced Orobanche foetida infestation in faba bean (Vicia faba)
exp_design: In the two cropping seasons of 2007–2008 and 2008–2009, the two faba bean genotypes were grown as a mono-crop (25 plants per m2) or inter-cropped in the same row with fenugreek (local landrace from Beja region, Tunisia) at plant densities (25 plants of faba bean and 40 fenugreek plants per m2) in a field naturally infested with O. foetida. In both seasons, the trial was implemented in different parts of the same field. The experimental design was a randomized complete block with four replications. Each genotype was sown in 4 rows, 4 m long, with 0.5 m inter-row spacing.

authors: Banik, P. and Sharma, R. C.
title: Yield and Resource Utilization Efficiency in Baby CornLegume-Intercropping System in the Eastern Plateau of India
exp_design: Each experiment had 13 treatments arrangement with 3 replications in a randomized complete block design. Each plot size was 6 × 3 m.
time_raw: Experiments were conducted during the rainy seasons of two consecutive years (2003 and 2004). Baby corn (Zea mays L. cv. VL-16), soybean (Glycine max cv. Alankar), green gram (Phaseolus aureus Roxb. cv. B-105), black gram (Vigna mungo Roxb. cv. T-9), and groundnut (Arachis hypogea cv. GG-2) were sown on June 18, 2003 and June 24, 2004. Baby corn was harvested on September 8, 2003 and September 11, 2004, whereas Green gram and black gram were harvested on September 15, 2003 and September 29, 2004. Soybean and groundnut were harvested on October 4, 2003 and October 15, 2004.
C_subpractice_description_raw: Baby corn sown at 60 cm spacing as monocrop
T_subpractice_description_raw: One row of soybean sown at 30 cm spacing in between of two rows of baby corn
C_tillage_subpractice_raw: power tiller ploughing followed by harrowing
T_tillage_subpractice_raw: power tiller ploughing followed by harrowing
T_intercrop_subpractice_raw: intercropping 2:1 row additive
T_intercrop_subpractice: Intercrop (N fixing and Non N fixing)
C_fert_subpractice_raw: The fertilizer schedule was 150:100:100 kg N, P2O5 and K2O ha−1 for monocropped and intercropped baby corn and 40:60:60 (N, P2O5, K2O) for monocropped legumes. Half of the N was applied through vermicompost (1.5–0.65–1.2) in baby corn as basal application. Proportionate fertilizers were also applied to intercropped legumes along the rows. One-fourth of nitrogen in the form of urea (46–0–0) and the whole amount of P2O5 and K2O in the form of single super phosphate (0–16–0) and muriate of potash (0–0–60) respectively were applied as basal and remaining one-fourth nitrogen was top dressed at 30 days after sowing (DAS). The total amount of N, P2O5, and K2O in the form of urea, SSP, and MOP was applied as basal in legumes.

The total amount of N, P2O5, and K2O in the form of urea, SSP, and MOP was applied as basal in legumes.

exp_design: In the two cropping seasons of 2007–2008 and 2008–2009, the two faba bean genotypes were grown as a mono-crop (25 plants per m2) or inter-cropped in the same row with fenugreek (local landrace from Beja region, Tunisia) at plant densities (25 plants of faba bean and 40 fenugreek plants per m2) in a field naturally infested with O. foetida. In both seasons, the trial was implemented in different parts of the same field. The experimental design was a randomized complete block with four replications. Each genotype was sown in 4 rows, 4 m long, with 0.5 m inter-row spacing.

time_raw: Experiments were conducted during the rainy seasons of two consecutive years (2003 and 2004). Baby corn (Zea mays L. cv. VL-16), soybean (Glycine max cv. Alankar), green gram (Phaseolus aureus Roxb. cv. B-105), black gram (Vigna mungo Roxb. cv. T-9), and groundnut (Arachis hypogea cv. GG-2) were sown on June 18, 2003 and June 24, 2004. Baby corn was harvested on September 8, 2003 and September 11, 2004, whereas Green gram and black gram were harvested on September 15, 2003 and September 29, 2004. Soybean and groundnut were harvested on October 4, 2003 and October 15, 2004.

T_intercrop_subpractice_raw: intercropping 2:1 row additive
T_intercrop_subpractice: Intercrop (N fixing and Non N fixing)
C_fert_subpractice_raw: The fertilizer schedule was 150:100:100 kg N, P2O5 and K2O ha−1 for monocropped and intercropped baby corn and 40:60:60 (N, P2O5, K2O) for monocropped legumes. Half of the N was applied through vermicompost (1.5–0.65–1.2) in baby corn as basal application. Proportionate fertilizers were also applied to intercropped legumes along the rows. One-fourth of nitrogen in the form of urea (46–0–0) and the whole amount of P2O5 and K2O in the form of single super phosphate (0–16–0) and muriate of potash (0–0–60) respectively were applied as basal and remaining one-fourth nitrogen was top dressed at 30 days after sowing (DAS). The total amount of N, P2O5, and K2O in the form of urea, SSP, and MOP was applied as basal in legumes.

title: Yield and Resource Utilization Efficiency in Baby CornLegume-Intercropping System in the Eastern Plateau of India
exp_design: Each experiment had 13 treatments arrangement with 3 replications in a randomized complete block design. Each plot size was 6 × 3 m.
time_raw: Experiments were conducted during the rainy seasons of two consecutive years (2003 and 2004). Baby corn (Zea mays L. cv. VL-16), soybean (Glycine max cv. Alankar), green gram (Phaseolus aureus Roxb. cv. B-105), black gram (Vigna mungo Roxb. cv. T-9), and groundnut (Arachis hypogea cv. GG-2) were sown on June 18, 2003 and June 24, 2004. Baby corn was harvested on September 8, 2003 and September 11, 2004, whereas Green gram and black gram were harvested on September 15, 2003 and September 29, 2004. Soybean and groundnut were harvested on October 4, 2003 and October 15, 2004.
C_subpractice_description_raw: Soybean sown at 30 cm spacing as monocrop
T_subpractice_description_raw: One row of soybean sown at 30 cm spacing in between of two rows of baby corn
C_tillage_subpractice_raw: power tiller ploughing followed by harrowing
T_tillage_subpractice_raw: power tiller ploughing followed by harrowing
T_intercrop_subpractice_raw: intercropping 2:1 row additive
T_intercrop_subpractice: Intercrop (N fixing and Non N fixing)
C_fert_subpractice_raw: The fertilizer schedule was 150:100:100 kg N, P2O5 and K2O ha−1 for monocropped and intercropped baby corn and 40:60:60 (N, P2O5, K2O) for monocropped legumes. Half of the N was applied through vermicompost (1.5–0.65–1.2) in baby corn as basal application. Proportionate fertilizers were also applied to intercropped legumes along the rows. One-fourth of nitrogen in the form of urea (46–0–0) and the whole amount of P2O5 and K2O in the form of single super phosphate (0–16–0) and muriate of potash (0–0–60) respectively were applied as basal and remaining one-fourth nitrogen was top dressed at 30 days after sowing (DAS). The total amount of N, P2O5, and K2O in the form of urea, SSP, and MOP was applied as basal in legumes.

The total amount of N, P2O5, and K2O in the form of urea, SSP, and MOP was applied as basal in legumes.
